newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mark slips, French shares up in early trade.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mark slips, French shares up in early trade.

text.p: The mark slipped against other European currencies and was weak against the dollar in early trade on Tuesday amid concern that a European single currency will not match its strength.
French stocks, however, added to the previous day's surprise gains as investors and traders awaited details of the new Socialist-led government.
Elsewhere, the London stock market showed limited losses, while Frankfurt was higher.

The dollar held on to its gains against the mark on market perceptions that the left's victory in the French parliamentary elections could lead to broad membership of a euro currency from the planned 1999 start date.
Against the U.S. currency, the mark traded around 1.7270, near Monday's lower levels, but it weakened to around 3.3720 French francs from 3.3740 late Monday.
Socialist Elisabeth Guigou, tipped for office in the new Paris government, said her party would respect the start date for European economic and monetary union.

Traders said if a broadly-based euro was launched on time without really tough measures to back it, rather than a delay which could prompt funds to flood back into the mark, it would be good news for the dollar.

"We know the Socialists want to go ahead on time but we know they're not so committed to actually meeting the criteria themselves -- that's underpinning the dollar," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at SGST.
A row between the Bundesbank and Bonn over plans to revalue the central bank's assets to help Germany qualify for EMU has also undermined the mark.

"The gold debacle and the French elections are the overriding focus and are making people think the euro will be a soft currency," said Mark Geddes, economist at ABN Amro. "This will keep the mark under pressure."
On Tuesday a German Finance Ministry spokeswoman, denying a report by the weekly news magazine Stern, said Germany had no plans to sell gold from the reserves.

The dollar, meanwhile, weakened against the yen after being unsettled by a market rumour that influential Japanese finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said the yen might gain to 103 per dollar from just under 116 now. But traders were sceptical.
"They've got (the yen) more or less where they want it now. Why rock the boat by making statements?" said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe.

Currency analysts felt there was little scope for the dollar to extend recent gains much without more shock news but said U.S. data later in the week could push the dollar above its 1997 peak of 1.7389 marks.
A stronger than expected National Association of Purchasing Managers' Index for May on Monday showed a U.S. economy benefiting from strong orders and subdued inflation.
U.S. April leading indicators figures are due at 1400 GMT but the main market focus is on May non-farm payrolls figures on Friday.
If these are strong, they would boost market expectations of higher U.S. interest rates at the next Federal Reserve policy-making meeting in July. But many economists have cut their forecasts.

French shares followed Monday's rollercoaster ride with early gains of around one percent as the previous day's biggest losers, banking shares and privatisation stocks, rebounded and bonds gained. BNP and Lagardere were early leaders.
The London stock market, Europe's biggest, opened steady, with a weak overnight performance on Wall Street countered by higher bonds and a revival in bank shares.
But it later slipped a little on interest rate fears ahead of a key British central bank monetary meeting on Thursday and the U.S. jobs data.
"With Wall Street easier, uncertainty about rates ahead of the (monetary) meeting later this week and the budget coming up on July 2, we're bound for a setback," said one senior dealer.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 41.64 points to 7,289.40 on Monday as investors sold blue chips to buy smaller companies and bonds rose.
The Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei average closed at a new high for 1997, up 111.31 points or 0.54 percent at 20,563.16.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7265 marks and 115.80 yen, compared with 1.7266 and 116.63 in late European trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was down 9.6 points or 0.21 percent at 4,553.2.
PARIS - The CAC 40 was up 23.99 points or 0.92 percent at 2,625.44. FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 10.72 points or 0.30 percent at 3,616.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $343.80 an ounce in the morning, compared with the previous London close of $344.05.
